title: US Revokes Visa of Bolivia’s Attorney General for Investigating Cerimedo
author: SinEmbargo Staff
content:
_This article by[SinEmbargo
Staff](https://www.sinembargo.mx/author/redaccion/) originally appeared in the
[September 29, 2026 edition of
SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4878824/eu-le-quita-la-visa-al-fiscal-
de-bolivia-por-investigar-la-red-corrupta-de-cerimedo/), a Mexican independent
digital news outlet._

**Mexico City, September 29 (SinEmbargo).—** The United States government
yesterday revoked the visa of Bolivia's Attorney General, **Roger Mariaca** ,
who is leading the investigation into Argentine consultant and La Derecha
Diario founder Fernando Cerimedo over the attempted femicide of Nadia Beller,
money laundering, usurping of functions, and other crimes.

"Mariaca, elected in 2024 to a six-year term as Attorney General under the
presidency of former leftist Luis Arce, and previously state prosecutor in
Santa Cruz, abused his public office by soliciting and accepting bribes to
facilitate drug trafficking and help violent criminals evade justice," the
U.S. State Department said in a statement.

In response, Mariaca rejected Washington's accusations and demanded respect
for his country's sovereignty, arguing that the U.S. decision amounts to an
attempt to interfere in the Attorney General's Office's investigations:
"Cooperation, yes; interference, no. Dialogue, yes; imposition, no. Respect
between states, yes; interference in our institutions, no," he said at a press
conference held yesterday in Sucre, seat of Bolivia's judicial branch.

> [Post by @Ollie_Vargas_ on
> X](https://twitter.com/Ollie_Vargas_/status/2104769537795326393)

During the press conference, Bolivia's Attorney General warned that the
Attorney General's Office's investigations will continue despite possible
political repercussions, both domestic and international. He specifically
addressed the case against Fernando Cerimedo, whose significance, he said,
must not become an obstacle to establishing the facts: "We also know that some
investigations have implications that go beyond national borders — the so-
called Cerimedo case, for example, has generated concern and repercussions
across different political spheres, but no political pressure, domestic or
international, can become an impediment to clarifying facts that must be
investigated," he said.

![Nadia Beller alongside Fernando Cerimedo.](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/09/2026-09-29-bolivia-attorney-general-visa-
cerimedo-02-nadia-cerimedo.jpg)Photo: SinEmbargo

Mariaca said his country recognizes the decisions adopted by other nations
within their own jurisdictions, but demanded reciprocity toward Bolivian
institutions. He questioned why accusations coming from abroad should cast
doubt on his performance as head of the Attorney General's Office: "We cannot
accept that the work I have been carrying out as Attorney General […] be
called into question by decisions or statements coming from abroad," he said.

The official also defended his record and argued that any accusation against
him should be clarified through the proper procedures, without damaging his
reputation before the facts are established. He distinguished between
diplomatic differences and actions that, in his view, seek to condition the
work of judicial authorities: "We can have differences, we can be critical, we
can express disagreements — that's part of relations between democratic
states. But it's one thing to express a position and quite another to try to
condition, interfere with, or affect the work of a sovereign institution like
the Attorney General's Office," he said.

He also stressed that he will hold his position against any measure he
considers retaliation for carrying out his responsibilities.

> If doing my duty, defending the independence of our institutions, and
> upholding Bolivia's sovereignty now means facing pressure or retaliation, I
> will take on that responsibility, because public service cannot be held
> hostage by fear.
>
> Roger Mariaca, Attorney General of Bolivia
